scenes.tts: The first film built a Punnett square for purple-flowered parents. Why might their real offspring counts miss its predicted ratio? A square gives each new plant a chance. A real group records what happened after those separate chances played out.
scenes.caption: The first film built a Punnett square for Pp parents. Why might their real offspring counts miss its predicted ratio? A square gives each new plant a chance. A real group records what happened after those separate chances played out.
scenes.visual: Reuse the first film's COLOR MAP exactly: purple = P and purple phenotype; cream = p and white phenotype; teal = paths and grid; gold = prediction; grey = neutral structure. The familiar Pp-by-Pp grid fills the left. On the right, an empty row of flower slots waits. A gold prediction marker hovers above while the slots gently pulse.
scenes.narration: The first film built a Punnett square for Pp parents. Why might their real offspring counts miss its predicted ratio? A square gives each new plant a chance. A real group records what happened after those separate chances played out.

scenes.visual: Brief title 'Why Real Counts Wander' appears between the carried grid and empty flower row. Both remain moving softly behind the title.

scenes.tts: Think of the square as a chance map, not a packing list. For every new offspring, one box is selected by the parents' allele contributions. Then the process starts again. Earlier flowers do not remove boxes or force later results. The map resets without remembering the last selection.
scenes.caption: Think of the square as a chance map, not a packing list. For every new offspring, one box is selected by the parents’ allele contributions. Then the process starts again. Earlier flowers do not remove boxes or force later results. The map resets without remembering the last selection.
scenes.visual: A teal selector travels across the four grid boxes and lands on one. A matching flower grows in the first slot. The selector returns to the full grid before moving again. No box disappears. A packing-list icon appears and crosses out. On-screen label: 'new chance each time'.
scenes.narration: Think of the square as a chance map, not a packing list. For every new offspring, one box is selected by the parents’ allele contributions. Then the process starts again. Earlier flowers do not remove boxes or force later results. The map resets without remembering the last selection.

scenes.tts: Watch a small computed example. Several selectors land, and flowers fill the short row. The colors form an uneven group. That does not make the square wrong. A small group leaves plenty of room for chance to swing the count. Another short run could lean differently.
scenes.caption: Watch a small computed example. Several selectors land, and flowers fill the short row. The colors form an uneven group. That does not make the square wrong. A small group leaves plenty of room for chance to swing the count. Another short run could lean differently.
scenes.visual: Label the panel 'computed example'. Use a fixed, precomputed sequence, not random animation. The selector fills a short row with an uneven mix of purple and white flowers. Bars rise beside the row. A gold target stays fixed while the observed marker wobbles away from it. Keep every label large and high-contrast.
scenes.narration: Watch a small computed example. Several selectors land, and flowers fill the short row. The colors form an uneven group. That does not make the square wrong. A small group leaves plenty of room for chance to swing the count. Another short run could lean differently.

scenes.tts: The short row has leaned toward one color. The next slot is still empty. Does the earlier run force the next flower to balance the group, or does the same chance map apply again? Make your prediction.
scenes.caption: The short row has leaned toward one color. The next slot is still empty. Does the earlier run force the next flower to balance the group, or does the same chance map apply again? Make your prediction.
scenes.visual: Carry the short computed row forward. Enlarge the empty next slot. Two arrows appear: one from the earlier flowers labelled 'force a balance?' and one from the unchanged grid labelled 'same chance map?'. The selector circles all grid boxes slowly.
scenes.narration: The short row has leaned toward one color. The next slot is still empty. Does the earlier run force the next flower to balance the group, or does the same chance map apply again? Make your prediction.

scenes.visual: Hold both choices and the empty slot. The selector continues a slow loop around the unchanged Punnett square. No result appears during the pause.

scenes.tts: The same chance map applies again. The next result is not a correction chosen by the earlier results. Each offspring is a separate chance. The group may move nearer the prediction or farther away before later results add more evidence.
scenes.caption: The same chance map applies again. The next result is not a correction chosen by the earlier results. Each offspring is a separate chance. The group may move nearer the prediction or farther away before later results add more evidence.
scenes.visual: Erase the 'force a balance?' arrow. The selector lands using the next item in the precomputed sequence, and a flower fills the slot. The observed marker moves but does not snap to the gold target. A label appears: 'separate chance'.
scenes.narration: The same chance map applies again. The next result is not a correction chosen by the earlier results. Each offspring is a separate chance. The group may move nearer the prediction or farther away before later results add more evidence.

scenes.tts: Now extend the computed run. More flower slots stream in while the bars rescale. The observed share still wiggles, but its swings usually shrink. With more separate outcomes, an unusual short streak has less control over the whole group. The curve approaches its target unevenly, not in a straight march.
scenes.caption: Now extend the computed run. More flower slots stream in while the bars rescale. The observed share still wiggles, but its swings usually shrink. With more separate outcomes, an unusual short streak has less control over the whole group. The curve approaches its target unevenly, not in a straight march.
scenes.visual: Transform the short row into a long conveyor of flower dots. Beside it, plot a computed running white share from the same fixed sequence. Label the curve 'computed example'. A gold horizontal target remains fixed; the cream curve (white share) wiggles widely early and more narrowly later. Axes carry on-screen numbers only.
scenes.narration: Now extend the computed run. More flower slots stream in while the bars rescale. The observed share still wiggles, but its swings usually shrink. With more separate outcomes, an unusual short streak has less control over the whole group. The curve approaches its target unevenly, not in a straight march.

scenes.tts: Mendel tested the pattern with real pea plants. He counted offspring for several traits, not just one small family. Place each dominant-to-recessive ratio beside the square's target. The rows gather near the target, but they do not land exactly together.
scenes.caption: Mendel tested the pattern with real pea plants. He counted offspring for several traits, not just one small family. Place each dominant-to-recessive ratio beside the square’s target. The rows gather near the target, but they do not land exactly together.
scenes.visual: The computed curve slides away. Transform the gold target into a horizontal ratio scale marked on screen. Seven pea-trait rows enter one at a time, each a dot labelled with its trait name only: no ratio numbers, no counts (two ratios are a lesson exercise). Mark the scale only at 3 : 1. Each dot stops near the target. Label the panel 'Mendel's counts'; do not label any dot exact or rejected.
scenes.narration: Mendel tested the pattern with real pea plants. He counted offspring for several traits, not just one small family. Place each dominant-to-recessive ratio beside the square’s target. The rows gather near the target, but they do not land exactly together.

scenes.tts: That spread is the evidence to examine. A prediction is useful when many real results gather near it, even without an exact match. No single row must sit exactly on the target. In the lesson, you will compare counts, ratios and group sizes yourself.
scenes.caption: That spread is the evidence to examine. A prediction is useful when many real results gather near it, even without an exact match. No single row must sit exactly on the target. In the lesson, you will compare counts, ratios and group sizes yourself.
scenes.visual: Keep all seven dots, labelled by trait name only. A three-part reading guide grows beside the panel: 'counts', then 'ratios', then 'group sizes', each with an empty box to fill in the lesson. Do not show totals or highlight any one row.
scenes.narration: That spread is the evidence to examine. A prediction is useful when many real results gather near it, even without an exact match. No single row must sit exactly on the target. In the lesson, you will compare counts, ratios and group sizes yourself.

scenes.tts: The square remains a one-gene model. Weather, soil, lost seeds, and more complex inheritance are outside it. Within its scope, it gives a clear target for repeated outcomes. Larger groups usually reveal that target more clearly than small groups do.
scenes.caption: The square remains a one-gene model. Weather, soil, lost seeds, and more complex inheritance are outside it. Within its scope, it gives a clear target for repeated outcomes. Larger groups usually reveal that target more clearly than small groups do.
scenes.visual: The ratio panel folds back into the framed one-gene Punnett square. Outside the frame, simple grey icons for weather, soil and lost seeds appear under 'outside this model'. Inside, a small group marker wobbles widely and a large group marker stays nearer the gold target. Label both 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: The square remains a one-gene model. Weather, soil, lost seeds, and more complex inheritance are outside it. Within its scope, it gives a clear target for repeated outcomes. Larger groups usually reveal that target more clearly than small groups do.

scenes.visual: End card shows one line only: 'Larger groups usually come closer to a Punnett square’s predicted ratio.' Behind it, the computed running-share curve continues a gentle motion near the gold target.
